title: Tool-calling interop: naming normalizer + OpenAI vs legacy functions shim
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket designs and implements a lightweight interoperability shim and naming-normalizer that allows Redwood API users to call tools using both OpenAI-style tool schemas and our older 'legacy functions' payloads. Goal: enable backwards-compatible client behavior without forcing immediate changes to customer prompts or SDKs, while preserving streaming & structured-output semantics and avoiding regressions in deterministic routing and cost accounting.

Problem statement:
- Some customers have migrated to OpenAI-style tool calling (name + parameters JSON schema) while older integrations still send legacy 'functions' shapes or different naming conventions (camelCase vs snake_case, full.namespace names, or local aliases).
- We need a server-side compatibility layer that: normalizes tool/function names and parameter shapes, supports streaming of tool outputs and function return content, preserves structured-output (JSON) behavior, and ensures telemetry and billing attribution map to canonical model/tool names.

Deliverables:
1) Naming normalizer rules and canonical registry mapping (server-side lookup table + update flow).
2) A small, deterministic shim that accepts both OpenAI-style tool call payloads and legacy functions payloads, performs name mapping, parameter name normalization (snake_case <-> camelCase best-effort), and returns a unified internal call envelope.
3) Streaming semantics: shim must passthrough streaming token events from tools (when applicable) and still emit structured output completion markers usable by downstream parsers.
4) Migration guide for customers and SDK updates (Node/Python examples).
5) Tests: unit/integ tests covering name collisions, ambiguous mappings, parameter type coercion, and performance microbenchmarks.

Design notes (high-level):
- We will maintain a canonical tool registry keyed by canonical_name (e.g., "search.documents.v1") with aliases list (e.g., ["searchDocuments", "search_docs"]). The registry is stored in the control plane DB and cached in the serving layer with a TTL.
- Name resolution flow: request arrives -> extract tool/function name -> consult in-memory alias map -> if multiple matches, evaluate disambiguation rules (priority: exact match > scoped match > last-used per-customer) -> if unresolved and client provided schema, attempt best-effort match using Levenshtein threshold and parameter shape similarity -> fallback to rejecting with clear error.
- Parameter normalization: we will normalize keys by converting common cases (camelCase <-> snake_case) and coerce numeric/string types when safe. We will NOT attempt deep schema morphing (e.g., changing nested object schemas) in this phase.
- Streaming behavior: when tool execution is streaming, the shim will attach metadata tokens to preserve tool identity and canonical name, and will emit an initial tool-call-start event followed by token events and a tool-call-end event. Structured JSON completions are preserved by marking the final event with "structured_output": "true" when a JSON blob was returned.
- Logging/telemetry: all shimmed calls must include an annotation mapping to the canonical tool name for cost attribution and per-tool SLO dashboards.

Backward-compat constraints and safety checks:
- We will not silently change parameter semantics for critical operations (e.g., deletion APIs) — special-case blacklist for high-risk tools requiring explicit opt-in to coercions.
- Ambiguous name mappings will generate a warning in response header (and an observation in Console) and require explicit alias listing within customer settings for resolution.

API Examples (normalized):
- OpenAI-style incoming: {"tool": {"name": "searchDocuments" , "schema": { ... } }, "args": {...}} -> shim maps to canonical_name "search.documents.v1" and converts args keys.
- Legacy incoming: {"function_name": "search_documents", "params": {...}} -> shim maps function_name -> canonical_name and converts params keys accordingly.

Acceptance criteria (must be strings):
- "Canonical registry exists and is queryable by serving layer"
- "Shim maps OpenAI-style and legacy payloads to the same internal envelope"
- "Streaming tool outputs preserve token-level events and structured-output markers"
- "No >5% p99 latency increase in median request path for non-shimmed calls (benchmarked)"
- "SDK migration examples added to docs and included in redwood-js/redwood-py PRs"
- "E2E tests for ambiguous alias resolution and parameter normalization"

Implementation tasks (ordered):
- "Design doc: publish canonical registry schema and alias rules (confluence: /redwood/docs/tool-interop-registry)"
- "Server: implement alias lookup and name-normalizer cache in runtime mux layer"
- "Shim: implement payload normalizer for OpenAI-style tools and legacy functions"
- "Streaming: add tool-call-start / token / tool-call-end events and structured marker"
- "Telemetry: add canonical_name tag to billing and tracing spans"
- "SDKs: add examples and a helper function normalizeToolCall() in redwood-js and redwood-py"
- "Tests: unit + integration + perf microbenchmarks"
- "Docs: migration guide and Console alerting for ambiguous mappings"

Dependencies:
- "ENG-6140: control-plane registry DB migration (must land first)"
- "PM-489: decide default alias policy for third-party models"

Risks and mitigations:
- "Risk: accidental routing to wrong tool when aliases overlap. Mitigation: conservative default — fail with a clear error and guidance unless customer opt-in to auto-resolve aliases. Also surface Console approval flow."
- "Risk: performance impact on hot request paths. Mitigation: local in-memory cache + lock-free lookup and feature flag to disable shim globally per-tenant."
- "Risk: subtle structured-output changes causing client parsing breakages. Mitigation: preserve final JSON blob without re-serialization where possible and include validation step in shim."

Rollout plan:
- "Feature-flagged beta for selected customers (start with a small cohort using legacy functions)"
- "Console: create a banner and alias-management UI in Console to let customers approve automatic mappings"
- "Gradual global rollout over 4 weeks conditioned on error rates and perf metrics"

Comments and progress log (chronological):

- "2025-02-12 Marco Li: Spiked a prototype of alias lookup in the serving mux. Local perf impact appears <1.2x on microbenchmarks. Pushing prototype PR for early review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/2567"
- "2025-02-14 Design review (Dana Ortiz): Suggests adding per-tenant alias override UI and explicit audit trail for alias approvals. Added to implementation tasks."
- "2025-02-18 Security review (Kunal Mehta): Flagged high-risk endpoints for which parameter coercion must be disabled by default. Added blacklist as a config."
- "2025-02-20 Marco Li: Implemented streaming event markers and integrated with token pipeline. Unit tests added."
- "2025-02-24 QA (Elena Rossi): Found an edge case where nested parameter arrays lose index ordering after a naive normalization pass. Reworked normalizer to preserve array ordering and added tests."
- "2025-02-27 Marco Li: Submitted PR for shim + registry integration. Requesting review from infra and product. https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/2599"
- "2025-02-28 Product (Ben Carter): Reviewed migration guide draft. Requested clearer examples of failure modes and recommended a short SDK helper to convert legacy to OpenAI-style payloads."

Current blockers:
- "Control-plane migration ENG-6140 still in flight (DB schema change for alias registry). Expected ETA 2025-03-03."
- "Final decision needed from PM on default alias resolution policy (auto-merge vs explicit opt-in). PM lead: Ben Carter."

Acceptance test pointers and where to look in CI:
- "Integration tests: tests/integration/test_tool_interop.py in serving repo (branch: eng/ENG-7821-shim)"
- "Perf harness: perf/tool-interop-bench in infra repo"

Next steps (short term):
- "Land registry DB migration (ENG-6140)"
- "Address PM decision and update the Console UX task"
- "Complete code review and merge feature-flagged shim behind runtime flag"
